protocol.description:
This experimental protocol lets an authorized Wayland surface receive viewer positions relative to the physical rectangle on which the compositor presents it. A client can use those positions to render a view-dependent portal while remaining an ordinary Wayland client.
This protocol is not stable and currently makes no compatibility promise. Once a version is deployed as a compatibility commitment, its wire ABI is immutable: interface version bumps may only append compatible requests and events, and an incompatible revision requires a new interface name.
The initial HypXRland implementation deliberately advertises no rendering capability and never activates a viewpoint. The requests and events below reserve the intended version-1 synchronization shape so clients can be developed without mistaking this transport-only implementation for working viewpoint feedback.
Viewer motion is sensitive data. A client request is not authorization; compositors must apply explicit user policy before sending samples.

interface.name: hypxr_viewpoint_manager_v1
interface.description: Creates at most one live viewpoint object for a wl_surface owned by the requesting client.

entry.name: invalid_surface
entry.summary: the wl_surface is invalid or belongs to another client

entry.name: already_constructed
entry.summary: the wl_surface already has a live viewpoint object

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. Viewpoint objects created from it remain valid.

request.name: get_viewpoint

description.summary: create a viewpoint object for a surface

request.description: Create a viewpoint object associated with surface. The compositor sends capabilities before any other event on the new object.

interface.name: hypxr_viewpoint_v1
interface.description:
A viewpoint object is initially inactive. The client declares its capabilities and enables feedback; the compositor either activates it or reports why it remains inactive.
Destroying the associated wl_surface makes this object inert. The compositor sends inactive with surface_destroyed, and all subsequent requests except destroy have no effect.

entry.name: invalid_state
entry.summary: a request is not valid in the current state

entry.name: invalid_capabilities
entry.summary: the capability mask contains unknown bits

entry.name: invalid_sample
entry.summary: the sample or activation identifier is invalid

entry.name: none
entry.summary: no packed stereo layout is available

entry.name: sbs
entry.summary: full side-by-side stereo

entry.name: hsbs
entry.summary: half side-by-side stereo

entry.name: tab
entry.summary: full top-and-bottom stereo

entry.name: htab
entry.summary: half top-and-bottom stereo

entry.name: none
entry.summary: no rendering guarantee is available

entry.name: pair_latched
entry.summary: both eyes are rendered from one sample and simulation state

entry.name: monotonic_timestamps
entry.summary: sample and target timestamps use CLOCK_MONOTONIC nanoseconds

entry.name: disabled
entry.summary: the client disabled feedback

entry.name: not_supported
entry.summary: feedback is not implemented or available

entry.name: surface_destroyed
entry.summary: the associated wl_surface was destroyed

entry.name: not_authorized
entry.summary: user policy did not authorize this surface

entry.name: not_eligible
entry.summary: the surface is not currently presentation-eligible

entry.name: xr_inactive
entry.summary: the XR session is not active

entry.name: tracking_lost
entry.summary: required tracking data is invalid

entry.name: superseded
entry.summary: another surface owns this presentation rectangle

entry.name: positions_valid
entry.summary: all advertised eye positions are valid

entry.name: sample_time_valid
entry.summary: sample_time is valid

entry.name: target_time_valid
entry.summary: target_time is valid

request.name: set_capabilities
request.description: layouts is a mask of layout values. flags is a mask of capability values. This state applies to subsequent activation attempts.

request.name: set_enabled
request.description: enabled must be zero or one. Enabling is a request, not authorization.

arg.name: enabled
arg.summary: one to request feedback, zero to disable it

request.name: rendered

description.summary: associate a sample with the next surface commit

request.description: The identified sample applies to the next wl_surface commit carrying a newly attached non-null buffer. Both words use network-independent semantic high/low ordering.

event.name: capabilities
event.description: layouts and flags contain only behavior the compositor can currently provide. Zero masks are valid and mean that this object cannot activate.

event.name: active
event.description: The content rectangle has the given physical size in micrometers. geometry_id changes whenever that rectangle's calibration changes.

event.name: sample
event.description:
Eye points are signed micrometers in a content-local frame whose origin is the content center, +X is right, +Y is up, and +Z points out of the visible surface toward the viewer. Timestamps are CLOCK_MONOTONIC nanoseconds only when the corresponding sample_flag is present.
Every sample sets positions_valid and has a view_count of one or two. All positions named by view_count are valid as one atomic unit. When view_count is one, right_x_um, right_y_um, and right_z_um must be zero. Invalid tracking is reported with inactive.tracking_lost instead of a partial or invalid sample.

arg.name: view_count
arg.summary: one or two valid eye points

event.name: inactive
event.description: Samples from epoch are no longer valid. Epoch is zero if this object has never activated.
